recentItems.description:
In this flashback clip, we revisit Bloodhound Q50 opening up to VladTV about the tragic loss of Bloodhound Lil Jeff. On June 8, 2024, Lil Jeff was killed, leaving a void in Chicago’s rap scene and in the lives of those who knew him personally. Q50 reflected on the close bond he shared with Jeff, describing him as more than just a friend, but as a brother figure who was part of his everyday life. He spoke candidly about the emotional impact of Jeff’s death, revealing that he broke down in tears after learning the news.

The conversation also touched on allegations surrounding Jeff’s alleged involvement in a high-profile case involving the deaths of two high school students. While Jeff was linked to the incident by some reports, another individual was charged in connection with the killings. Q50 also addressed a claim from Trenches News that Lil Jeff wanted to emulate the late King Von, pushing back on the comparison and emphasizing that Jeff was carving out his own path.

recentItems.title: TK Kirkland on Boosie Saying Rod Wave's $100K Gift Wasn't Enough: He'll Regret That Later (Part 2)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 1: https://youtu.be/rRLJVBMJt3I
--------
In this VladTV interview, comedian and entrepreneur T.K. Kirkland reacts to the dispute between Boosie and Rod Wave over sampled music from Boosie’s early catalog. Vlad explains how Rod Wave reportedly cleared the records through Trill Entertainment, which owns much of Boosie’s older material, then offered Boosie $100,000 as a gesture of respect despite not being legally required to pay him directly. When Boosie said the amount wasn’t enough, the situation turned into a social media back-and-forth.

Kirkland breaks down why he believes “all money is good money” and warns that turning down free income can become a future regret. Vlad also compares the situation to his past interview-rate disagreement with Boosie, discussing market value, respect for money, and how artists navigate business in hip-hop. The conversation touches on Rod Wave, Trill Entertainment, Rickey Smiley, 60 Minutes, and the realities of music ownership.

Chingy on Sidney Starr, Nore, 2Pac, Keefe D, Janet Jackson, Charlamagne (Full Interview)
recentItems.description:

https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
--------
Chingy sits down with VladTV for a wide-ranging conversation about music industry politics, the Keefe D trial, past controversies, and the lessons he's learned throughout more than two decades in the business.
Chingy opens up about the lack of authenticity he has experienced in entertainment, including people promising appearances or collaborations only to give him the runaround later. Vlad suggests creators start putting reciprocal appearances into contracts, complete with financial penalties when someone fails to honor their agreement.
The conversation turns to Keefe D's conviction in the Tupac Shakur murder case, with Chingy questioning whether the full story has been revealed and sharing his theories surrounding the night Tupac was killed. Vlad also explains what he knows about the death of Outlawz member Yaki Kadafi and addresses some of the theories that have surrounded the case for decades.
Chingy then revisits the controversy involving Sidney Starr, maintaining that allegations made about him years ago were fabricated for attention. They also discuss Starr's more recent legal troubles and how false or damaging claims can follow entertainers throughout their careers.
Later, Chingy focuses on his next chapter in music, introducing Gold Chain Confessions and what he calls Luxury Midwestern Soul, a sound centered around peace, maturity, and wellness. He and Vlad also discuss the resurgence of St. Louis hip-hop, including Sexyy Red, Nelly, the St. Lunatics, and Metro Boomin.
Chingy concludes with important lessons about publishing, mechanical royalties, contracts, and protecting yourself financially. After beginning his career with a $9,000 deal, he explains how understanding the business eventually helped him secure a $3 million publishing agreement.

Max B opens up to VladTV about a pivotal chapter in his life and career, from resolving past tension with DJ Kay Slay and Papoose to the rise of Coke Wave and Coke Wave 2 with French Montana. The Harlem rapper reflects on industry relationships involving Jim Jones, 50 Cent, Remy Ma, and Kay Slay before detailing the New Jersey case that changed everything. He discusses Gina Conway’s 15-year plea for manslaughter and armed robbery, her testimony, and why he says he rejected a 10-year deal rather than testify against his co-defendant. Max B also recalls the guilty verdict, the 75-year sentence, jail after trial, and how he studied appeals, PCR, and post-conviction relief in hopes of finding a legal path forward.

In this VladTV interview, Trap Lore Ross analyzes the Lil Durk court case, explaining why he believes reasonable doubt became a key factor for the jury. Ross discusses alleged murder-for-hire testimony involving Quando Rondo, claims about unpaid money, Flocka’s testimony, Boonie, Jam, Ronnie’s car movements, hotel and condo locations, and references to OTF’s *Loyal Bros* album and “Federal Freestyle.” He also weighs the importance of Durk’s phone allegedly not being at key locations and why the lack of clear payment evidence may have helped the defense.

The conversation then turns to the tense atmosphere outside and inside court, where Ross says a Durk supporter threatened to punch him in his “big Jew nose.” Ross responds to the insult, discusses Doodie Lo sharing a message reportedly from Lil Durk telling fans to leave him alone, and reflects on threats made on federal grounds.

--------
Nicholas Irving joins Shawn Prez for a blunt conversation on America’s security 25 years after September 11, 2001. Reflecting on the legacy of 9/11, the Twin Towers, Osama bin Laden, TSA procedures, government surveillance, and post-9/11 policy, Irving argues the United States is not necessarily safer than it was on September 10, 2001.

Rather than focusing only on foreign threats, Irving warns that today’s biggest vulnerabilities may come from within — political division, social breakdown, and the possibility of a coordinated attack targeting public spaces or major events. He questions whether expanded security measures have truly stopped terrorism, while pointing to government overreach and a fractured national culture as signs of deeper risk.

In this candid interview, Shawn Prez presses Irving on whether another large-scale attack could happen in modern America, and Irving gives a sobering assessment of where the country stands today.

Interview by: Shawn Prez

Part 1: https://youtu.be/K7__iCx2ghE
--------
Criminal defense attorney Bradford Cohen sits down with Vlad to discuss his work for Travis Scott following the rapper’s 2024 Miami Beach arrest connected to disorderly intoxication and trespassing allegations. Cohen breaks down why he viewed the case as minor from the start, explaining that prosecutors ultimately pursued a trespass charge after an incident near a yacht dock.

According to Cohen, his team moved quickly, sending an investigator to photograph the area the day after the arrest. Those images, he says, showed there were no “no trespassing” signs posted at the dock. Cohen also details how Travis Scott allegedly left when police asked him to, then returned for a forgotten backpack before being arrested. The attorney says the case was dismissed after he challenged later photos presented by the state.

Cohen also shares his personal impression of Travis Scott and mentions crossing paths with him in Monaco.

recentItems.title: Norteño Shot Caller Mario Sanchez on Why D4vd Deserves the Death Penalty Instead of Life (Part 8)
recentItems.description:

Part 1: https://youtu.be/-pWadYhoSkc
--------
Vlad sits down with Norteño figure Mario Sanchez for a blunt discussion on California’s death penalty, wrongful convictions, and the controversial D4vd (David) case involving allegations tied to the death of a 14-year-old girl. Sanchez explains why he supports capital punishment in certain cases, especially when minors and sexual allegations are involved, but stresses that the evidence must be strong enough to justify a conviction. The conversation also revisits the state’s last execution of Tookie Williams, debates raised with Judge Mathis, Timothy McVeigh’s federal bombing case, DNA evidence, unreliable eyewitness identifications, and the broader risk of executing an innocent person. Vlad also compares how prosecutors pursue life sentences versus death penalty cases, referencing the Lil Durk case as an example of a high-profile murder case not seeking execution. Watch the full exchange for Sanchez’s take on justice, accountability, and life without parole.
